synopsis: Chapter 11 and the glossary agree that CARLA is open source and its code is MIT-licensed; the glossary also describes it as free [f8463, f15900]. Chapter 11 notes that CARLA has two current release lines, without naming them in the supplied facts [f8463]. The glossary classifies MIT as permissive alongside Project Chrono’s BSD-3 and the Apache 2.0 licenses for Isaac Sim and Gazebo [f15924]. These licenses allow commercial use, modification and redistribution provided the original copyright notice is retained, and do not require companies to publish their own changes [f15925, f15927].

relations.note: Both identify CARLA as open source with MIT-licensed code.
